Herbert Gorman, The Place Called Dagon.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/herbert-gorman/the-place-called-dagon

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Herbert Gorman, the author, died 1954 (Wikidata Q5894712, date of death 1954).

First publication of the text used: 1927 (SE colophon: 'The Place Called Dagon was published in 1927 by Herbert Gorman.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1927, before 1931. The edition's own statement of rights, quoted below, says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the possible countries of first publication are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Nothing in the facts points to France, Spain, Mexico, Colombia or Russia/USSR. The last person to die among those named above died in 1954, and each of these countries has a term of life + 70 years or less, so the work is public domain in each of them.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
